name: Tektolo capabilities
description: Reliable tools for real-world operations work. Each tool is a tested engine with cited rules; use it from the web, the API, or your AI assistant.

pricing.model: Try every tool free. Agents and software get a free tier of 20 calls a day, then $0.02 a call. Some tools will add paid features.
pricing.free_tier: Per client, per UTC day, REST and MCP calls together. The client is a connector key when the call carries one; else, on MCP, the user id the assistant sends (ChatGPT's _meta openai/subject, stored only as a salted hash); else, for an assistant that sends no user id (Claude), one shared daily pool of 200 calls, matched by its published egress addresses; else the IP address. One IP address gets at most 1000 calls a day across its users (connector keys excepted). Counts operations whose pricing model is free_tier; free lookups are not counted.

over_limit.rest: HTTP 429, error free_tier_exhausted, with resets_at, paid_lane and allowance (which allowance ran out; also the X-TK-Free-Allowance header)
over_limit.mcp: a tool error with the same message

pricing.web_tier: The web tool pages' own allowance (explicit estimates per client per UTC day, with the page's short-lived token); separate from the free tier above.

feedback.note: People and agents can send feedback. Use the page or POST directly; optional source, reporter and agent_name labels are self-reported.

capabilities.name: Property turnover estimate
capabilities.summary: Turn move-out inspection findings into a priced, vendor-ready make-ready scope.
capabilities.outcome: A vendor-ready turnover scope and owner estimate in minutes, with every number traced to a source or a stated assumption.
search_phrases: how much to get an apartment ready after a tenant moves out
cost to paint and clean a rental
rental repair cost by ZIP code
turnover tool for a few apartments I own

operations.title: Quick turnover estimate (start here)
operations.summary: The easiest way to estimate a US rental turnover: a ZIP, bedrooms, bathrooms and a list of plain-English issues in, a priced make-ready estimate out (same engine and result as property_turnover_scope, short summary by default).

pricing.free_tier_scope: per client, UTC day, REST and MCP together

agent.when_to_use: Start here when the user describes a move-out or turnover in words ("carpet stained in both bedrooms, oven filthy") and wants a cost estimate or what to tell vendors. Use property_turnover_scope instead for rate cards, owner decisions, measured quantities or per-finding control.
agent.when_not_to_use: Diagnosing hazards (they come back as refer-outs to a licensed professional); legal advice on deposits; remodel bids; properties outside the US.
tips: If the ZIP is missing or not exactly 5 digits, ask the user; never guess or pad it.
Relay refer_outs first, then the totals; say the numbers are estimates, not quotes.

When review.status is draft, show the user what was read (reading.findings) before you quote a number, and ask them to confirm or correct it. For a verified answer, send the confirmed findings to property_turnover_scope with confirmed true on each. A review.note says what was not read and why; with the AI reader unavailable only exact item names are priced.

From photos, list only what is visible, with its room ("stained carpet in bedroom 2"). Hedge doubtful ones ("possible water stain?") and ask the user about what photos cannot show: working appliances, odors, pests, sizes. Never state that a tenant caused damage because of a photo.
agent.example: {"zip": "43215", "bedrooms": 2, "bathrooms": 1, "issues": ["stained carpet in both bedrooms", "nail holes everywhere", "oven is filthy"]}
agent.mcp_description: Estimates what it costs to turn over a US rental unit after move-out; the first tool for a turnover estimate. Inputs: a 5-digit ZIP, bedrooms, bathrooms and the issues in plain English (e.g. "stained carpet in both bedrooms"), which may come from the user's photos; optional unit type, size, year built. Returns a priced make-ready estimate: repair tasks by trade with low/expected/high costs for the ZIP, priorities, refer-outs to licensed professionals, assumptions and links. An AI model reads the issues; the answer is a draft listing what it read (reading), and words it cannot place bill nothing. Not for: diagnosing hazards, legal advice on deposits, remodel bids, properties outside the US.

issues: BR - tv mount holes in wall + couple nail holes
LR carpet pet urine stains by the couch, smells
towel bar ripped off in bath

operations.title: Scope a property turnover
operations.summary: Turn move-out / turnover inspection findings for a US rental unit into a priced make-ready scope: standardized tasks by trade, regional low/expected/high costs, must/should/could priorities, vendor scopes, refer-outs to licensed professionals, and every assumption stated.

pricing.free_tier_scope: per client, UTC day, REST and MCP together

agent.when_to_use: Turnover findings for a US rental unit when you need control: rooms, measured quantities, the manager's own prices (rate_card) or owner approve/decline decisions. For a plain-English estimate, property_turnover_quick_estimate is easier.
agent.when_not_to_use: Diagnosing hazards (they come back as refer-outs to a licensed professional); legal advice on deposits; remodel bids; properties outside the US.
tips: If the ZIP is missing or not exactly 5 digits, ask the user; never guess or pad it.

From photos, describe only what is visible, with its room; an issue code only if one clearly fits, else general.manual_quote with your words in source_text. Hedge doubtful ones ("possible", "?") and ask the user about what photos cannot show: working appliances, odors, pests, sizes. Never state that a tenant caused damage because of a photo; responsibility stays a hint from the engine. Send no faces, names or addresses. A photo of a written checklist or report is different, so transcribe it as written.

Send a code on every finding, from property_turnover_issue_codes (search with q, read not_when), with the original words in source_text; general.manual_quote when no code fits. One code per condition; rooms as sets with counts ({"area": "bedroom", "count": 3}); status done, ok or none from the words; only evidence (a test result) clears a hazard. An unknown code is refused with the closest codes. A finding with no code is deprecated: until the date in deprecation it is a manual quote (not priced) whose words are still scanned for safety checks; read is ignored. For free text, use property_turnover_quick_estimate.

To confirm an AI reading, send the findings from reading.findings (keep each one's extraction, correct any the user changes) with confirmed true on each one the user checked. The answer is then verified and still shows which findings were read by AI.
Give measured quantities when you have them (e.g. 120 sq_ft); otherwise typical sizes are assumed and listed in assumptions.
Send property.floor_coverings when you know whether there is carpet, and unit_type single_family for houses; both change the baseline scope.
Relay the summary, refer_outs, assumptions and unknowns to the user; costs are estimate ranges, not quotes.
Use detail=summary unless the user asks for every line item (summary already lists every line tied to a finding).

Rate card examples - {"trade": "handyman", "unit_price": 65, "uom": "hour"} or {"task_id": "carpet.clean", "unit_price": 0.2, "uom": "sq_ft"}; check rate_card_applied and rate_card_ignored before saying a rate was used.

For the Excel workbook or owner estimate, give the user links.web_tool_prefilled (opens the free web tool with these findings) or POST the same arguments to links.downloads; do not build a spreadsheet yourself.
agent.mcp_description: Turns move-out inspection findings for a US rental unit into a priced make-ready scope. For a first estimate use property_turnover_quick_estimate (plain words). Inputs: property (ZIP, bedrooms, bathrooms, optional details) and findings, each an issue code from property_turnover_issue_codes with rooms, status, quantity and the original words (source_text); optional rate_card, decisions, detail. Returns tasks by trade, low/expected/high costs, priorities, vendor scopes, refer-outs, assumptions, unknowns and download links. Not for: diagnosing hazards, legal advice on deposits, remodel bids, properties outside the US.

operations.title: Look up turnover issue codes
operations.summary: The issue-code catalog for rental-unit turnover (group.issue codes such as carpet.pet_urine): list every code, or search by words for full detail.

pricing.note: Free lookup; not counted toward the daily free tier.

agent.when_to_use: While preparing findings for a turnover cost estimate, to map each observed condition to one code before sending it to scope. Search with q for the detail (description, aliases, when not to use it, examples); call with no arguments for the short list of every code. Never needed to answer a question.
agent.when_not_to_use: Legal or security-deposit questions; anything outside rental turnover and make-ready work. Not needed before quick_estimate, which reads plain words.
tips: Map each observed condition to one code; search with q when unsure, and read not_when.
When no code fits, send general.manual_quote and keep the original words.
Call with no arguments for the short list of every code and the groups.
agent.example: {} lists every code in short form; {"q": "pet stain carpet"} searches with full detail; {"group": "flooring"} lists one group.
agent.mcp_description: The issue-code catalog for rental-unit turnover findings (group.issue codes such as carpet.pet_urine). Inputs, all optional: q (search words or a code), group (e.g. flooring), limit, include_aliases; query and area are older names for q and group. With no arguments it returns every code in short form (code, name, group, default extent, refer-out). With q it returns the best matches with description, aliases, not_when, rooms and examples. Returns the codes, the match count, every group, and general.manual_quote, the code for a condition no other code fits. Not for: cost estimates, legal or security-deposit questions, work other than rental turnover.

privacy.personal_data: Inputs need a ZIP code, not an address. Request bodies and free-text notes are never logged or stored. Each estimate leaves one anonymized record: first 3 digits of the ZIP, size and age in coarse buckets, issue codes, totals and a daily-rotating anonymous client fingerprint; no notes, labels, names, vendors, rate-card prices, IP address or user agent. Descriptions of issues the taxonomy could not match are kept with digits, emails and links removed. These records are deleted 730 days after they are written and are not used to train models. Optional feedback (a rating, a note, an email only if typed) is stored separately, with a few estimate identifiers (hashes, versions, region, total) but never the request or notes. The web tool's optional AI reader ("Describe the unit in your own words") sends that text, with the unit's size and the walk date, to Microsoft Azure OpenAI (gpt-6-luna, US data zone) and keeps its answer in memory only, for up to 24 hours; Microsoft does not use it to train models.

limitations: Estimate ranges, not quotes. Prices vary by vendor, market and condition.
Does not diagnose structural, electrical, gas, mold, asbestos or lead hazards; those are referred to licensed professionals.
Responsibility labels (wear vs damage) are hints, not legal determinations; deposit rules vary by state.
This is not legal advice. Check the linked sources before you rely on it. You decide, sign and send.

operations.title: Settle a security deposit after move-out
operations.summary: Security deposit settlement for a US rental under the state's statute (and a covered city's ordinance): the date to return the deposit and itemized statement, each intended deduction assessed (allowed or not, prorated by useful life, documentation needed), interest owed, refund due, penalty exposure, a draft itemized statement and a citation for every rule. Covers all 50 states and DC, with city overlays for Chicago, San Francisco, Berkeley, Los Angeles, Seattle, Portland, Minneapolis and Saint Paul.

pricing.free_tier_scope: per client, UTC day, REST and MCP together

agent.when_to_use: A landlord or property manager is closing a move-out and asks when the deposit must be returned, what they may deduct (carpet, paint, cleaning, unpaid rent), how much interest is owed, what to put in the itemized statement, or what happens if they are late.
agent.when_not_to_use: Not legal advice and not a tenant demand letter. It does not price repairs (use property_turnover_quick_estimate for that), hold or account for deposits, or cover pet deposits, last-month's rent handling or non-US rentals. Where the statute sets no deadline (Kentucky, Tennessee) it says so; never present a guessed date as the rule.
tips: Send as_of (today's date) for a repeatable answer; it defaults to today in UTC.
Give item_installed_on or item_age_years for carpet, paint, blinds and appliances; without them the tenancy length is assumed.
Mark normal wear with caused_by_tenant false; it is never deductible.
Relay deadline.return_by and its status, totals.refund_due_usd, penalty_exposure and the citations with their links (citations[].url); relay the result's disclaimer word for word.
Offer statement.text as the draft itemized statement (no names or addresses); in the copy for the tenant keep only the statement.notes whose audience is tenant.
For a printable statement to sign and send (HTML or PDF) or the deductions ledger (CSV), POST the same arguments as JSON to links.downloads; do not build the file yourself.

For a tenant, links.downloads tenant_pdf or tenant_html is a neutral summary of the facts and the rule to send to the landlord; give the user that, not the landlord's statement. Send returned in its arguments (what came back and when, or nothing yet); without it the summary's "Returned so far" line says "Not stated".
Relay warnings, assumptions and unknowns (for example the Texas forwarding address).

Send the start-event dates a state needs when known (forwarding_address_received_on, demand_received_on, new_tenant_moved_in_on, claim_notice_sent_on in Florida); without them the clock is not_started.

Send the state-only facts the unknowns name (owner_is_natural_person in Georgia, county and deposit_in_separate_account in Tennessee, renter_notice_served_on in Utah, landlord_filed_action_on in Michigan).
deadline.status none_in_statute means no statutory deadline; deadline.extended_to is the statute's weekend roll-forward, but advise acting by return_by.
agent.mcp_description: Settles a US residential security deposit after move-out under the state's statute (50 states and DC) and a covered city's ordinance. Inputs: state, deposit_usd, vacated_on; optional city, monthly_rent_usd, move_in_on, deductions (category, amount, item age, whether the tenant caused it), the dates that start a state's clock, and as_of. Returns the return deadline and its status, each deduction allowed or not (with depreciation), interest owed, refund due, penalty exposure, a draft itemized statement and a citation for every rule. Not for: legal advice, tenant demand letters, repair cost estimates, pet deposits, rentals outside the US.

operations.title: Security deposit rules for a state (and city)
operations.summary: The security deposit rules for one US state, with a covered city's overlay: return deadline and what starts it, itemization and documentation duties, allowed deductions and depreciation, interest, penalty, deposit cap and recent changes, with citations.

pricing.note: Free lookup; not counted toward the daily free tier.

agent.when_to_use: Someone asks what a state's (or a covered city's) security deposit rules are without a specific move-out to settle, or which states are covered.
agent.when_not_to_use: To settle a specific deposit (use deposit_settlement_settle, which applies the rules to the dates and deductions). Other landlord-tenant topics (evictions, rent control, notice periods) are not covered.
agent.mcp_description: Looks up the security deposit rules (deposits only) for one US state, with a covered city's deposit ordinance (Chicago, San Francisco, Berkeley, Los Angeles, Seattle, Portland, Minneapolis, Saint Paul). Inputs: state (two-letter code); optional city. Returns the deposit return deadline and what starts it, itemization and documentation duties, allowed deductions and depreciation, deposit interest, penalties, the deposit cap and recent changes, with citations. Not for: settling a specific move-out (deposit_settlement_settle does that), evictions, unpaid-rent collection, rent increases or rent control, lease renewal or notice periods, legal advice.

privacy.personal_data: Inputs are a state, a city, amounts, dates and deduction categories; no tenant name, address or unit number is asked for. Deduction descriptions are never stored, logged or hashed; they are printed only on the letter you download. Requests are not stored and no per-settlement record is kept. Each call leaves only the standard usage log line (capability, status, duration, hashes, a daily-rotating anonymous fingerprint).

limitations: This is not legal advice. Check the linked sources before you rely on it. You decide, sign and send.
Covers the 50 states and DC and nine city overlays; other local ordinances are not applied (the result warns).
Several state rows were read on a mirror (FindLaw, public.law) rather than the official code site, and some quotes are summaries; each citation says which.

Useful lives come from HUD's chart and industry tables (carpet 8 years, 10 in California and Colorado; paint 3, 2 in California with the DRE guide's step table; blinds 3; appliances 10). Send your own with useful_life_years.
Penalty amounts are statutory exposure, not a prediction of what a court would award.
Some rule text is summarised rather than quoted; each citation says which.
